Weight-only quantization addresses the memory bottleneck exposed after redundant compute is removed, linking architectural reuse with hardware-level efficiency. |

Nearline behavior encodings condition an online action decoder through cross-attention. Incremental updates and per-request caching amortize history processing, keeping request-time work less dependent on the full behavior-sequence length. |

Each layer queries raw multimodal user tokens, computes relevance matches and updates that fixed-size state, rather than carrying a large sequence-shaped hidden tensor through every layer. Shared user tokens across candidates further reduce memory duplication while retaining access to detailed histories. |

A lightweight head reads item–position scores from the language model's prefill states, and an assignment algorithm produces a valid order in a constant number of model passes. This replaces sequential token decoding, though score construction and assignment still depend on the candidate set. |

| <a id="paper-2609-23111"></a>**Inherit4Rec: Parameter Inheritance for Efficient Scaling of Recommendation Models**<br>Reading priority: Read first | Kuaishou Technology; Shenzhen Technology University; City University of Hong Kong | arXiv | 2026 | `MoE` `Training Efficiency` `Sparse Activation` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23111) | Inherit4Rec supports capacity growth and dense-to-sparse conversion without restarting recommender training. Function-preserving hybrid growth and asymmetric training retain update continuity; co-activation-aware expert partitioning supports sparse conversion. Experiments on KuaiRand-1K and an industrial short-video dataset report gains over the evaluated inheritance baselines, motivating reuse of trained rankers under serving budgets. This is an inheritance recipe rather than a fitted scaling law. |
| <a id="paper-2609-12399"></a>**OneLA: Scaling Linear-Attention Decoding to Large Beams in Generative Recommendation**<br>Reading priority: Read first | Kuaishou Technology; The University of Hong Kong; Peking University | arXiv | 2026 | `Attention` `Serving` `Generative Rec` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12399) | OneLA reduces the cost of large-beam generative recommendation by sharing one prompt-derived linear-attention state and retaining compact records of divergent beam transitions. An ancestry index and fused GPU kernel avoid copying full recurrent states. The paper reports 1.54–2.46x full-model decode-forward speedups in its tested configurations, suggesting a reusable state-sharing pattern for short-output, wide-beam retrieval; this is not a measured whole-service latency gain. |
